newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE MUST ACT FAST OR FACE CALAMITY, MIN SAYS.
newsitem.headline: GREECE MUST ACT FAST OR FACE CALAMITY, MIN SAYS.

text.p: Greece has two years to get its economic house in order or face a calamity, Interior and Public Administration Minister Alexandros Papadopoulos told the daily newswpaper "Ta Nea".
The next two years will be tough and problems which have been dodged in the past must be address before Economic and Monetary Union, Papadopoulos, a former well-respected finance minister said.
"We haven't followed the example of other countries who were (once) at the same level of development as us, such as Portugal, Ireland and Spain," he said.

"We now have two years left in which to avert facing a calamity... Greece needs some good house cleaning and all have to be aware that we will not make it if we do not accept that 1997 and 1998 will be tough years, years of sacrifices", he added.
The restructuring of public service and local and regional adminstration will be the lynchpin in the effort to put Greece's house in order.
Efforts must concentrate on getting municipalities out of the red and on using funds better.
"The state will be present to ensure the law is applied and that the rules of proper administration are conducted. Spending on wages cannot exceed 50-60 percent of regular revenues," he said.

Legislation for the computerisation of public sector services, as well as radical changes to the public servants' code of conduct, changes to the disciplinary system, will all be submitted to parliament by the end of this year, he said. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
